text: Let's just say that this wasnt a great experience. I'll start with the fact that Hannah, the hostest was very rude. 2. They initially told us a 15 minute wait and it ended up being over 1 hr. I was travelling with my wife and 3 daughters one of which being 4 months old, this was a complete inconvenience. I will say though that the manager, Steve did come over and rectify, but definitely not a good place on a Saturday night with an infant. p.s. I don't see Hannah's future as a hostess being too bright!

I think the food here is delicious. Although service has definitely slowed since they moved I still appreciate the effort. Try their huarache dish it is soo good and the few margaritas I've tried so far are also very yum! I wish them continued success!

Mr Lee is a very nice business person running a great business.He is about to introduce a vegetarian sandwich made with Michaels savory seitan. A all natural vegan and vegetarian sandwich which is very popular in the Phila region and areas.You must taste his creations and you will see this is truly a delicious no fat low sodium all natural tasting veggie steak sandwich. Be ready for the next best sandwich coming out of Phila with Mr Lees SEITAN STEAK SANDWICH. He is using the best tasting Seitan on the planet being made from a local vendor and seitan maker for the past 20 years or so.Please try his creations and support the local farmers and vendors and eat healthy.Learn where your food is coming from and care for your enviornment support local eat local.Michael

Very difficult to make a reservation for normal dinner hours. Made reservation 2.5 weeks in advance. It's because the space is so small, uncomfortably so. It feels like someone will knock over glasses as they walk by. No separate gluten free menu, no indications on the menu. Server explained some options. As an Italian restaurant, I was surprised that they didn't have one gf pasta or pizza available. The food I had was great. Cheeseboard, branzino and pistachio/raspberry cake. Non-gf guest had pasta and salted caramel budino. Only gluten part of that is the chocolate crust on the bottom. Here's hoping they can provide a gf version in the future.

Everything was delicious. I had the Cajun pasta, jambalaya, and crawfish etouffe and they were all delicious. The only reason I'm not giving 5 stars is because of how expensive the food is. We also waited a long time for the jambalaya. Our waitress was super nice and let us try a little alligator since it was our first time in New Orleans. There was also a live band and was super cool. Very good atmosphere and food!

I tried this place for the first time a few months ago. I ordered a gyro through drive through. When I checked it, it had very little sauce and only on one fourth of the gyro. I asked for extra sauce and they said I had to pay more. I explained it was my first time there and that the sauce was not on the whole gyro and they said something about how they have to make money too and that it would be either 75 cents or a dollar more (can't remember.) Bad customer service. For the nearly ten dollars for just a sandwich and a stressful ordering experience I won't be back.

I really like Royal Tavern, but it can be VERY difficult to get a table here. Another one of those "go early or be willing to wait" places. Both of which are very hard if you're very hungry. The food is definitely worth waiting for, though.
Absolutely love this new stop in town. So cute, everything is delicious. The baristas are always smiling and suggesting their favorites. 110% recommend

Literally my favorite breakfast place on this planet. My saddest day ever was the day I moved from Philly and knew I would no longer be able to come here for brunch. The tiramisu french toast is out of this world, perfect texture, perfect amount of sweetness, literally they could do no wrong. I can't go to brunch and just eat dessert so I usually get the french toast and the breakfast burrito together so I can have salty and sweet combo at my meal. The breakfast burrito is pretty good too. I'm a vegetarian so I always sub the chorizo for the veggie sausage... best combo ever. The special coffees are always a must too. I usually just drink black coffee but its really hard to say no to these beautiful drinks. I have had the nutella latte and the salted caramel lattel, both were great and I would recommend either. Make sure you bring cash. They have an ATM but probably better to plan ahead to avoid any fees.

The main reason I'm giving two stars was because of the service. The waitress's attitude was less than desirable, she seemed tired and annoyed when we asked questions, because me and my boyfriend had never been there before. It got to the point where I just stopped communicating with her and she only addressed my boyfriend when checking up on us. She told me to "smile" because "it was the holidays". The food was delicious (bottom of the bowl) but due to the service I wouldn't step foot back in there. Servers can make or break an experience! I know because I am one.

This is a beautiful restaurant with delicious food. We love it here and wish we lived closer. I get the butter poached pad Thai and it is divine. The noodles are a bit bigger than I like for pad Thai but that's a minor thing. It's a little spicy which is unusual for pad Thai but it's still good. Hun gets the filet with the spinach and blue cheese dumplings and the cheese croquettes. Excellent! Had sushi this time (Maine roll and eel roll) but think next time we may skip that and try some other apps. Loved the crispy brussels. Shredded, crispy, and full of flavor. Want to try the edamame dumplings next time.

I just had appetizers like the empanada, tostones, and the pastel. Amazing! Tostones were big, tasty and not overfried. Pastel had a lot of flavor and the empanada, might have been a cheese/beef combination. All for under $12. All delicious! You Puertorican? Afraid this might not do it for you? Worry no longer! Delicious and great service!
What a major let down. Says open until 9p on Saturday but less than five of the places were actually open.
Great food, great service. I never have a complaint when i leave here. Try the ghost pepper chicken bites.

Came here for an outdoor dining experience (during "Phase Yellow" of social distancing) and we were thrilled with our experience. They were a little short staffed, but extremely kind and apologetic about it, and we didn't even feel they were understaffed... all of the food came out very timely. The tables were appropriately spaced and well cleaned. The restaurant gets 5 stars mostly for the food itself. The drinks were flavorful and delicious as well-- I recommend the Ginger Bird. Everything we had was excellent. We started with a Caesar salad, which was flavorful and well balanced with the amount of dressing. Then we had the whipped sheep's ricotta, which came with freshly baked sourdough bread. For our main entree, we had the pistache pizza, which absolutely unique and delicious. All of the flavors were well balanced. We also ordered a cannoli to go, but took a bite before leaving because we couldn't resist. I highly recommend you come enjoy a meal here, or order takeout if you feel more comfortable with that or want a night in with delicious food!

Went here for Beignets to compare it to Cafe Du Monde ( ). Liked them better. They were nice and hot and fresh and had the right amount of sugar. Be prepared to spend a lot of time here because the ordering is SLOW.. There were 4 parties in front of us and it took them 20 minutes to take their order. Once we put in the order the food came out in good time. If I wanted beignets I'd definitely go here again (just not during breakfast)..

This is such a great breakfast spot. Their bagels are always so fresh and delicious. Me and my boyfriend like to stop before we head into work some mornings. I love the nova lox. It's not over the top expensive like tho ya with smoked salmon usually are and you get a decent amount of it too. Cream cheese & smoked salmon on a bagel is one of my favorite breakfasts and they do it justice! The wait was a little bit long, considering that's all I got and my boyfriend only had a normal egg sandwich, but it wasn't the end of the world. The employees are also very friendly.

Found this place after running errands in South Philly and looking online for kabobs. Pros: the partitioned takeout containers that kept my hummus from my rice from my salad, the salad dressing, the hummus. Cons: the amount of food for the price Blah: the chicken of the chicken kabobs Very, very nice people work here. If I were to return, I'd try something else on the menu.

Every once in a while, you find a great little place that is so good, you want to keep it secret so hordes of hungry customers do not swarm into the place preventing you from getting incredible food. La Charrerria is such a place. They have a strong selection of tacos, along with more common items like arroz con pollo, fajitas and tamales. Amongst the shining stars on their menu are the "street food items"-- gorditas, harrachas and quesadillas all made with a homemade dough resembling arepas. Each of these are extremely flavorful as well as substantial. So far, our family tried, quesadillas, hurrachas, gorditas, tacos (traditional and American), huevos con chorizo, and chimichangas. Each item was well prepared with good quality meats (we tried grilled chicken, chorizo, asada, tinga, and ground beef), and all very tasty. Although smaller in size, the restaurant does provide wait service, and during our visits the service has been friendly and top-notch. La Charreria is definitely worth a visit, but please leave room for the rest of us

Wow this was proof that Texans can't BBQ it was at best a warm attempt at southern BBQ meat only had a slight smokey flavour, pulled pork was dry the slaw had zero dressing, the bean I spit out sweet garlic unpleasant taste,the potato salad the dressing was good ... the side ribs were whacked off and tossed on top of everything did I bother the owner by going in to buy food about as personable as getting bunched in the face,last when a person comes into your BBQ joint no take home sauce I give fired up a D- needs major improvements and to the pony tail goof go buy a personality there was only one BBQ king and he passed away four yrs.ago Smokey Joe would have told ya take your ass back to Texas
Stopped here after seeing the small place driving to work, it turned out being a hidden gem !!

I love coming up to Santa Barbara and I always love going to the Sand Bar. The service is great, the setting is great and the food is really good. The owner must know what he's doing because it truly is a well run restaurant. And there are so many restaurants to choose from. We always go to Sand Bar, every trip up! Wish we had one closer to Orange County and LA county. Just appreciate the fun people there. Management is great and it shows. We have always had great customer service. Thanks Sand Bar!!

Today, this is my favorite pizza spot. The pizza was delicious. We had the chicken pesto and the Jammers "o" riginal. They were both full of flavor. There are several different specials that you can choose from or you can even build your own. It doesn't hurt that you can also get a beer or glass of wine to go along with your pizza. The price is about right, the atmosphere is nice, family friendly and they even have seating outdoors. The sports fans would also like it here because the walls are adorned with big screen TVs. One more added plus for Theo's is the Pac-Man arcade game. Who doesn't love Pac-Man and pizza?

Growing up in an Italian home was great. The food my mother made was amazing and this place was the closest I have ever come to my moms cooking. The portions are large. Also the sauce is to die for. Keep up the good food and wine. I would give you 10 stars if I could. Good job Update just enjoyed this place pence again. If you want the best server you must ask for Ryan. His recommendations are spot on. From the wine to the food. Ryan, Ryan, Ryan. Wow great place.

interesting to read some of the other comments. its not really a chain, but a few stores owned by a few different people. To say that you'd go to Tres Amigos is a joke. True, I never recommend people to get the beef tacos, etc. The ground beef has never had any real flavor for me. Just ask them to make sure your beef dish is not "ground beef". The steak is ribeye, purchased each week, marinated and sliced on site. The beans are not out of a can. The salsa's are all made on site, and the queso dip. Like any place, business is off and the staff changes and moves on. Some of them dont even speak english well. I still have many many items on the menu i'd eat anytime. Its a regular stop for us - but Amigos (and we've eaten there over many years since don pablos opened) is NOT!

The Moon Under Water is a fun pub in downtown St. Petersburg. The atmosphere is there is a bit on the dark side, but it is offset with colorful flags and mirrors. We stopped for a late lunch but we were too early for Happy Hour, so the drinks were full price. They serve typical pub style food there, however, they also offer a variety of curry dishes that I have heard are very good, and other dishes that pay homage to British Colonial food style. I've never had curry before, and I wasn't about to try new flavors on this day. Instead, I opted for Jerk Chicken and fries. The jerk was great and the fries were firm and crispy. Hubby had a Shepherd's Pie and he said it was very good --very flavorful. Another member of our party had a beef pasty which was also very good. The pasty and the Shepherd's Pie were very filling, both diners leaving with a To go Box. All in all, a nice little pub to hang with friends or to have lunch or dinner!

The food is fantastic but if you dont have anything to do and nowhere to go know job to go to and have absolutely nothing else going on in your life then this is the place for your I literally have been waiting in like for 36 mins I'm starting to think something is wrong with me for even doing this. My husband asked me to pick up his dinner for him on my lunch break never again will I come here on my 30 min lunch break because this is absolutely ridiculous

This review is only for the Vietnamese iced coffee! It's amazing for all the real coffee lovers. It came sweetened with milk(I usually don't sweeten mine) but it tasted so good! I just had them add a little extra coffee and it was perfect! I hate waiting until they open at 11 to get it though!!

We live right around the corner, and while the price point here is slightly higher than Mona's, it's really one of our favourite Turkish places on earth!! First of all their Courtyard baba ghanoush (not the appetizer) and yes it's $12 but split it between you or go home and drown in it tomorrow - you KNOW you'll want to. It's like a lasagna with alternating layers of roasted eggplant (even a little charred and crunch at the ends) then a layer of baba, then fresh tomatoes, then herbs. Repeat. It's freakin heaven. Even my father, who doesn't really care for ethnic food, loves it. There are other appetizers I've tried zaalook? which are wonderful but it's all about the baba. We usually get a chicken kebab sandwich (beautifully seared, never too dry) and a gyro sandwich (not easy to split between two, but we do). There's also the Adana kebab which is a mixture of beef and lamb. I'm actually starting to miss it as I write this review. The owners are waiting for their liquor license at last glimpse, but I think the baba plate would be great to split between 3 or 4 with cocktails, like a WAY higher end plate of nachos. One of the don't miss spots in New Orleans.

The food is good, but Half Moon keeps on letting me down. Drove all the way over for pick-up, got home and realized that I was missing something. Unfortunately, not the first time this has happened--I should have learned my lesson and checked before I left. I hate to say it, but I think that's too many strikes. I won't be back.

This Vietnamese/Chinese eatery has been around for many years. It is not as flashy as some of the newer places I love to frequent, but it is enough and comfortable in its subtlety. Plus, the flavor is what's important and there's nothing subtle about the flavors going on here! Plus, plus, the owners are very kind and appreciate all support of their business that (literally) serves edible art. #Getlostindiana
Very nice small space with great service. Had the Rajas con Crema Quesadilla and Bean Taco. Both very satisfying!

It's called L.A. Jackson for a reason guys. Coming from L.A. this scene is very typical of what you'd find from a trendy hotspot: beautiful patrons, upscale environment, central bar to ogle and people-watch your heart out, and a sweeping view of Nashville's downtown skyline. We arrived at 11:30pm on a Friday night, no line, no wait for the elevator so we went right up to the rooftop. The security guard was friendly and we got in without any issues (so NOT L.A. lol) The space is separated by 2 main areas: Inside: perimeter lounge areas (first come, first served), round bar, and a teeny tiny dance floor. Outside: cafeteria-style tables, lounge seating, heat lamps, and a central lighted tree that sets the mood for a wild night out. $17 for a whisky on the rocks. $3 cheaper than L.A. standards, score!! Hahah If you're in town visiting and jonesing for something other than Broadway honky tonk bars- L.A. Jackson's rooftop bar is the SPOT. Leave the cowboy boots at home and don your BEST #ootd y'all. It's upscale-trendy dress attire and a bunch of beautiful peeps.

A short cab ride from the hotel, we arrived Morimoto's. The white exterior and gradual luminescence effect of the entrance reminded me of Agape Substance. To think that the restaurant has been around for almost 10 years I was wondering why it took me so long to go there. The restaurant was a contrast of white lighted with different colors and wood. I requested for a table at the bar so we could watch the chefs in action. Where we were seated it was a good view of everything. We started with a cocktail gin and yuzu a very refreshing drink and an interesting flavor from the yuzu that was distinct. We also ordered a sake to go with the 8 course dinner. 1st course was the toro tartare - mixed with fried shallots it was moulded in a cylinderical ring topped with some osetra caviar, around it was a soy-mirin sauce. The softness of the fish was contrasted with the crunchy caramelized flavor of the shallots. I enjoyed the flavors in the soy-mirin sauce that balanced the salt and sweet. 2nd course was a trio of Kumamoto oysters from Washington - each one topped with a different flavors starting with the gentle slightly jazzy Japanese orange salsa, the citrus cilantro ceviche had more punch and lastly finished with the stronger elements of fish sauce and jalapeno. I wished the oysters were bigger and perhaps not quite in season but Kumamoto's unique sweet brine was distinct. 3rd course was the whitefish carpaccio - while the fresh fish slices marinated in the yuzu-citrus soy mix and aromatic herbs of garlic, ginger and chives, it was finished Cantonese style with smoking hot oil. The treatment gave the fish an infused smokiness, together with the soy mix and aromatic herbs it was a very delectable dish. 4th course was the sashimi salad - fresh firm slices of yellowfin tuna cleverly paired with mixed green in a yuzu vinagrette. The yuzu, a gentle citrus flavor went blended well in a creamy sauce that was left you wanting more. At the intermezzo we had a palate cleanser of strawberry-ume-shiso soda it was an interesting palate cleanser using the Japanese plum that was salty and sour flavor. 5th course was the lobster epice - again I would say it was a Cantonese style dry rubbed spices on the lobster then a flash fry in deep hot oil, resulting in a nice smokiness and char from the spices yet leaving the lobster meat tender and juicy. The lobster itself was so good perhaps it didnt really need the western accompaniment of a chive cream. I missed the Singapore black pepper crab made this way but this lobster was a refined dish of that. Very tasty! 6th course was the Australian Waygu - we upgraded from American Kobe, the four slices of Australian Wagyu served raw with an oiled hot plate that the wagyu was barely swished a few times the condiments were a miso sauce and smoked sea salt fumakake it was so simple yet filled with rich flavors and textures. Of course I loved it. 7th course was an assortment of 5 nigiri sushi - premium quality fish slices were used in the nigiris there were Chutoro, stripe skip jack fish, orange clam, regular tuna and regular skip jack fish. This is what I call sushi! Last but least our 8th and final crouse was a Japanese cheesecake with peach compote and blueberry. The cheesecake was light and airy unlike the heavy ultra sweet American version the texture had an interesting quality that made you want more of it. I loved this cheesecake. Overall, we were very happy with the experience especially the food. For a $120 Omakase a well composed menu, we had many very high quality ingredients, something that was lacking in many overpriced Chef Tasting menus. The only gripe I had was that main server did not come across very sincere and had a slight attitude which was not pleasant. The other staff who served us at some point of the dinner were all very nice.

Carne Asada quesadilla is on point. Great mesquite flavor, salsas are tasty as well Small, divey place where the dining room is a little smoky from the grill, smells great! Great if your at TMC Labor & Delivery as its right across the street. Will be back for sure after the kiddo is born
Lekker, maar ze kunnen duidelijk hun 'succes' niet aan. Langzame tot zelfs slechte service. Zonde, er liepen zelf mensen weg omdat ze niet eens aangesproken werken bij binnenkomst.

Solid 4 stars restaurant. It s close to 4.5 stars. If the dining open, I would consider to dine here. During the pandemic, they only allow take out. There a few review indicated if you dine in, the food take some time to come out. I think it is a easy fix. We started with the Garlic Parmesan Chicken Wing. We don't like the fry and get the wing a la cart. The wing was perfectly done. I like the parmesan with oil on wing. It is delicious. We got the chicken waffle to star also. I thing the fried chicken strip is nothing special. But it do have good fried. The waffle is soft. May because I have it take home. Our entree is the smothered pork chop. It has good smothered gravy sauce on top. We also got the oxtail. The meat is fall off the bone. The oxtail was cook for sometime and soft to eat. Very good dish. From order to pick up is about 20 minutes. Not bad. Considering it is a good southern dishes.

Everything was very delicious. There was one problem & I was dinning with 4 other people who agreed; the steak knives were too dull. It took us forever to cut the fabulous (all different) cuts of meats.
What an amazing atmosphere! The food was delicious exclamation point in our server Jesse was the most outstanding person I've ever met!!!

Came here with family after an event in the area. We were here on a Tuesday night. I was impressed with how busy it was for a weekday night! We had to wait a little bit since we had a party of ten. The only downside is that there really isn't a waiting area, so we had to wait in the bar area, and with kids, uh yeah... I really love that when you order tap water, they bring you a glass container for the table. That was really neat. Felt like you were at some super fancy restaurant. One of their specials for the evening was a chicken cordon blue sandwich on a pretzel bun. That was a big hit with the table. Other meals included: flamethrower, "the hill", chicken and dumplings, and pasta with meatballs. Oh yeah, and grilled cheese. The food was good. The service was good. I can see going back here!

We found Edison's Food Lab online and through Yelp. It is a different and unique experience that you go into with an open mind. The menu choices are designed to stimulate the taste buds and try new combinations. We enjoyed it very much. The fried green tomato salad was my personal favorite , but our group all sampled a variety of items on the menu. The chicken club and chicken with waffle dish were both very good. Our server was great and we will definitely return.

I am still in search of that Wow restaurant on the Main Line - where its worth the price. Peppercorn almost got it right. Our apps were flavorful and the ambiance was lovely. Dinner lacked a bit of flavor. Service was slow and frustrating. Although it is nice to sit and take your time at dinner, especially when paying $36 for a lil piece of halibut, it was upsetting that we would not see our server for long periods of time. I want exceptional service and WOW flavors for the money. Did not happen here. The bus boy, Zach, paid more attention to us than our server.

I went on a Saturday around 6pm. The wait was really long about 45 minutes. They gave us a free beer thanking us for waiting. There were a lot of people there and the line moved at a decent speed. I ordered the pimento cheese burger. It has was a double burger with a fried green tomato, hot sauce aioli, and onions. It was really good. My husband ordered the boudin balls, he liked them but I did not. Even my picky child liked my burger so we will definitely be back and she liked my husband's Louie burger.

Nice little place to bring a family to eat. The setting is very nice, kinda of has a beachy feel to it. They specialize in seafood. Service was very good. I had the seafood pasta which was good. The prices were fairly reasonable. My only complaint is that I thought the portions were kind of small. Overall, nice spot to take family or take your date, I will be returning.

Came here for dinner with a few friends, it all started very nicley, the waitress was great. She is probably the only reason this place is getting 1 star and not 0. So dear Management please be good to your personnel.(I m not sure of her name, girl with curly hair and is an actress) Anyway, we came here not knowing what to order so just got a bunch of appetizers, none of which were particularly good, the Potatoe Leek soup was too salty, The sea bass had no flavor, the chicken could of had a bit more flavor to it. The lamb chops caused one of the people from our party a stomach ache. Over all the ambiance is nice, but the food is just not very good and overpriced for poor quality dishes. I wouldn't come back here and def would not recommend others to visit.

This is just another dimly lit Asian place serving asian fusion food. I just wasn't really feeling Suzy Wong's, maybe it was just an off day. I came here during restaurant week with a group of friends. It was kind of hard to find the restaurant at first because there wasn't any sign or light on that street! I ordered the crispy teriyaki pork belly, which was good, but had a little bit more fat than I had anticipated. But the non fatty portion was seared and seasoned really well! For the entree, I had the filet mignon, which was pretty good. For dessert, I had the thai ice cream, which wasn't what I had expected it to be. Some of my friends ordered, the strawberry cream cheese wontons and those were really good!!! Overall, I wasn't super impressed with the food at Suzy Wong's... Maybe it's because I went in with super high expectations but I definitely wouldn't mind stopping by again to give it a second chance.
I went with my girlfriend because she has been there before. I loved it! The burgers are amazing. I recommend it. The server was very attentive and friendly.

Holy crap this place is awesome! My husband and I stopped in on a whim just to grab a couple of cocktails and small plates, and now we're kicking ourselves for not staying and having a full dinner. Cocktails were solid, but the hummus and Jerusalem bagel absolutely blew us away, ridiculously delicious and very generous portions. I honestly think Olio ruined me for life, any other hummus, pita, or bagel I have that isn't from Olio is going to be a disappointment.

A bunch of us were staying in Philly for the Made in America festival and our hotel was only 10 minuets away from the terminal. We got there around 2PM expecting to get sandwiches... that was so naive. The line stretched out the door so we wound up getting something else. We got back the next day on Sunday around 10:30 PM when the line was a lot more reasonable. I had the roast pork with broc rabe and provolone. It was good, just not "Best sandwich in America" good. Would get it again if the line is reasonable.

Stopped in for drinks on a Saturday night, and the place was nearly empty. Ordered a Moscow Mule & a Mint Julep - which I thought were pretty basic drinks. They were way over priced for the little bit of alcohol they served over 90% crushed ice and they tasted terrible. These drinks, when made properly, are my favorites, but these were flat, tart, and basically watery lime juice in a sea of ice chips. After trying to get our bar tenders' attention for close to 5 mins, in an empty bar, it was painfully obvious she was ignoring us. We politely asked the her if we could exchange our drinks for beer. After a ton of attitude, and insinuations that we don't have the proper taste pallets to drink these beverages, and repeatedly asking the hostile bar tender for a manager, we walked away with beers. Management was understanding and accommodating when he was finally pulled into the messy situation. Overall left a bad taste in out mouths.

Slightly over priced and undersized rolls that lacked good presentation and any wow factor. The crunchy roll wasn't crunchy and the volcano roll lacked fire. Our server was very nice but I have no reason to return. I leave disappointed.

Hassan is the wonderful owner of Mood Cafe and he always puts together delicious concoctions made of fried crunchy things and fresh fruit and veggies. They even have meat chaats if you're feeling a little adventurous. They have like 19413 flavors of lassis and every one that I've tried has been delicious. I recommend this place to all of my friends and it is deserving of every 5 star review here. The line can get a little crazy during lunch, so I would recommend going during off hours to save time and effort.
Great food and drinks. If your in the area its def worth trying. I lovee the pineapple bowl and the table side guac is a nice touch

Not gonna lie, Asian restaurants will have bad to mediocre service and that's more normal in the Bay Area with the influx of Asian owned restaurants. That being said, the pho here is my favorite pho in all of Reno. I really enjoy their banh xeo that is only available on weekends. The pho is flavorful and they give you soo much meat and noodles in your bowl for the price. A medium is definitely more than enough to fill me up but I can't resist a good banh xeo either. The banh xeo is superr crispy. They definitely know how to make these but the ingredient preparation is a little time consuming for those who complain they run out or won't do it later. The actual making isn't that long and should be easy for them, but when they run low on shrimp/pork/other items in their dish, they probably only allocated so many. I also had their 3 bean dessert and their Vietnamese coffee. The dessert is good with the coconut milk, pretty typical in taste. The coffee is a bit sweeter but still strong.

Melt is a little confusing to me. If your main deal is waffles, I'm kind of expecting to have one hell of a waffle! I had the apple waffle and while it wasn't bad, I've had way better for cheaper. It's good to satisfy a sweet tooth (or to sober up which was my goal). The price wasn't *so* bad though and I did really enjoy their self-serve bottomless Mississippi Mud coffee with choose-your-own kitschy mug! I got out with a bill under $25 for an apple waffle, a wake-and-bake, and two bottomless coffees which is reasonable for me. Also my dining companion and I ended up leaving a little earlier than we usually would have because a very loud live band was setting up and live music isn't our jam. I just wanna eat waffles and drink coffee, not listen to a band play. Maybe not the most appropriate venue? But then again it's Cherokee St. so... Two stars for the coffee, one star for the waffle. I did have to go to the bar to pay my waiter but it looked like they were a little understaffed which is understandable. All the staff I interacted with were pleasant and helpful. I would go again if on Cherokee and craving breakfast but I wouldn't go out of my way to revisit.

We are from Texas and we eat a lot of tacos. But these tacos are the bomb. Also the smoked salsa is amazing. We tried the lamb, carnitas and chorizo tacos. They were all great, but my husband and I both felt like the carnitas were the star. And they are all LOADED with meat. I also tried a side of Mac & Cheese that was creamy, rich, and delicious. We tasted some brisket and lamb sausage. The brisket just about melts in your mouth and the lamb sausage was a pleasant explosion of flavors. We left stuffed and happy, and the prices were reasonable. Would definitely recommend

Only been for lunch but the dinner reviews sound wonderful. For lunch it's quiet and the menu is nice. I ordered the beet salad and it was fresh, crisp and sweet. I had it with an Earl Grey, the bar tender kept topping up my tea with hot water but in the end it was another teabag I needed. Weak tea is not for me. The decor was lovely, exposed brick, cool mural on the wall, modern furniture and you can see right into the kitchen. It's a cosy vibe, with bright light from the long windows looking right out onto 124 Street.

Last night we were looking for a place too eat. We almost exclusively eat in traditional Asian restaurants (my wife is Asian). So when I say traditional it means Asian Fusion is not really Asian and while I like American Asian foods we look for menus with traditional dishes also. While we live near Villanova we decided to pass by Pin Wei and Ping Pong to try Bamboo last night and happy with our new discovery. Bamboo is a traditional Chinese restaurant with a huge selection of traditional Chinese dishes as well as American Chinese. The place was full and mostly Asian people with just three European Americans. The food was very good - perfectly prepared and very fresh. I had hot and spicy lamb - two out of four chili hot on the menu scale. The waitress had a conversation with us on how hot and she toned it down a bit for me. My wife had a hard time choosing as the menu had so many good choices and she thoroughly enjoyed her dishes. Some have commented on service. This evening was very good. The staff were very considerate and attentive to the guests. I wonder about people with unrealistic expectations, looking for service like a Friday's or Applebee's where the training is national and food is tasteless. With a family run business the food is excellent, arrives when made and you need to interact like family - raising your hand and asking questions. For me the service at Bamboo was better than most Chinese Restaurants. All in all we are definitely coming back and highly recommend this restaurant.
A very rustic place but the staff very nice. I had the greens and they were on point delicious. My boys were full and satisfied. We will for sure go again when we visit New Orleans.

The food here is pretty good, if not a little on the pricey side. Classy atmosphere with a nice lay out. The staff definitely leaves a little too be desired. It was a busy night, so some understanding there, but the waitress didn't really seem too concerned with even getting our drinks out in a reasonable time. I'd still give it another chance based on the food alone.

This is one of those places that you drive long distances to try. I loved every minute of my drive home with a belly full of amazing food. The mac and cheese is phenomenal, add bacon on top of it and it's beyond amazing. Check this place out sometime, you won't regret it. Cheers.

So my wife ate here many months ago and was happy with everything. So we order a large pepperoni pizza, at 7:40 on a Thursday (I.e. Not late). 20 minutes later what we get is a cold pizza, obviously baked hours ago, that they just added a few bits of cheese on top to melt it. You can't even bake a pizza fresh? Dominoes would have better!! Check the pictures

Seriously amazing food!!! Seated right away as we had a reservation. It was a Saturday night and I wouldn't recommend going without one...we were seated near the host stand and people arriving at 630 without one were told an hour wait. Started w sangria which was tasty. The steak tartare was on point, although I ate it off the grilled bread because I am not used to it being on toast and didn't want to fill up on bread. Now for the super star. The tufoli. The homemade pasta was to die for. The pork ragu. The garlic. The broccoli rabe. The parmesan. The portion was a good size for me. I prefer quality over quantity any day of the week. I was full but didn't leave stuffed which is how I prefer to leave a meal. Service was good. It's not a large place and you could hear other conversations even without trying to eavesdrop, not a downfall just something to note (especially for the couple next to us who were bickering). I say go. And get the pasta.

Cafe Beignet was highly recommended from the chef instructor of my cooking class and omg when I tell you that he did NOT steer me wrong with this one! The beignets were absolutely fantastic. The size, the sweetness of the dough with the powered sugar and they were so fluffy. My only regret is that I didn't order a hot chocolate to go with it! I love the set up of the cafe and the decor was simple yet beautiful. There was even a man who set up his guitar to play which added another level of awesomeness to the ambiance. There are many places in NOLA to get beignets but make sure this is on your list near the TOP. The location we went to was in the French quarter and although the place was busy it was not overcrowded. Service was great too and we didn't wait long for the beignets at all. I enjoyed my experience here and I highly recommend it!

My husband and I came here last week because I craved yellow curry. I'm having a hard time finding Thai food that I'm used to having in Southern California. We started with chicken satay. It was good. I felt the portions were great for the price. For entrees we shared yellow curry, spicy fried rice, and drunken noodles. The yellow curry was not creamy and had a lighter curry flavor. It was okay. The chicken in it was tender and well sliced. The rice tasted charred and my husband and I both opted out of it. The drunken noodles were okay. I tasted more wok or oil than flavor of the noodles and spices. The service was outstanding. While we were there, there were only two tables so I'm not sure how it is on a busy night. The server was very friendly and quick to answer questions. Prices were reasonable as well. As for me, my quest continues.

I have only eaten here for breakfast/brunch & one time for dessert. For dessert I ordered the chocolate lava cake with ice cream & that was really really good!! The other time I was here for brunch and it was great! Staff and service are great and the inside is super cute. I got the tofu scramble bowl?? I think that's what it was called. Came with veggie sausage, tofu scramble, hollandaise sauce, and a biscuit somewhere in it lol. While I will def be back here to try an actual entree I think at the moment I do prefer the wild cow.
I ordered the fried clam strips, and they were nice size strips of clam. I also ordered the Grouper Bites and they were delicious.

Seriously was excited to try out a new Mexican spot closer to my house than Cafe Ynez. Disappointed doesn't begin to cut it. The nachos were the best thing we had and that's not saying much. The meat was all dry, the fajitas were just ok, the waitress was inattentive and it wasn't that busy for her level of ineptitude. The saving grace was that she noticed that I hated the tacos ilegales and she reordered them made the way I had expected them to come the first time. Separately the meats were moist and hot and good. Together, well refer to my previous comment on the meat. Long story short... we won't be back and I'm pissed at my SIL for suggesting it was anywhere near edible. Also, their mixer and accompanying items for making drinks are practically nonexistent when it comes to making anything other the cheap drink mix margaritas.

Took my family to lunch today, we all ordered the buffet. Well, they had two breadsticks, two pizza's with only a couple pieces left. So as we each had one, my husband had two, we waited for the gals to maybe cook some more, well they never did. One gal working had her friends show up and they ordered the buffet, she went and cooked them a pizza and they took the whole thing, then she went back into the back. We waited some more and they never set anymore out so we left. So we paid $6 each for 1 slice of pizza. We will never go back!

After eating at Graze for a few years with mostly positive experience, I recently was appalled by the offensiveness of one of their employees, toward me, and in front of the entire clientele. I ordered my regular, which I often order 3 or 4 times a week. It tasted very different than usual, so I sent it back. A cook came over and leaned in very close to me and began lecturing me on the risk I take when making modifications to a menu item and then said he would "this one time" do me the "favor" of remaking it. The modification I made was to add spicy tempeh to the Caesar wrap, which I have always paid extra for, and I usually ask for it to be extra spicy. The wrap only had about half the amount of kale Caesar in it compared to the usual amount (this had already begun to be a bit of an issue the last few times I had ordered the dish, but without the overt extra saltiness I discovered in my first bite) and the bite I took was extremely salty to the point that I almost had to spit it out. I've never sent anything back there, and have hardly ever sent back a dish in any restaurant, even when it wasn't good. But this was my regular at a place I would consider my local spot to eat when not cooking for myself. I have over 10 years experience in professional kitchens including being a lead cook/chef and kitchen manager and have done event cooking, private cheffing, and meal planning. I eventually found out that this cook was also one of the owners. He also told me that he only appreciated my business up until that day. I've never been so talked down to by an employee, let alone an owner of an establishment. All I wanted was the proper amount of kale put into my wrap when I sent it back. I didn't order a lecture or a demeaning and arrogant attitude. This guy turned what should have been a simple refire and non issue into a condescending spectacle. The guy tried emailing me an apology, but it was a veiled and phony one. It was really just a longer lecture on why I had been in the wrong with a lot of "mansplaining" vibe to it, with a $20 gift card attached. Gag me with a spoon! Why one of the owners other than the one who had been a total jerk didn't reach out to me, I do not know. What I want as a regular who has literally spent thousands of dollars at an establishment is a little bit of humble approach and understanding when they do something less than expected. I've had plenty of imperfect meals, and I've never left a negative review of any establishment in any way at any time. I have a habit of giving cooks the benefit of the doubt in many ways, because I have worked as a cook. I didn't even have yelp and have never used it until now. Every single thing this person expressed and how they did so was the opposite of how I've been instructed and trained to treat a client or customer. For years I have supported Graze and The Wild Cow, and I've always recommended these places to other people, as well as always tipping very well. And this guy has the nerve of marching over to me with a scowl and getting in my personal space without even a tinge of respect shown to a customer, and telling me that the lack of execution of the dish was my fault. Even though the food at Graze has usually been pretty good, this one person was able to leave a lasting bad taste in my mouth much worse than the wrap I bit into.

Absolutely love the food here, and have eaten in their dining room many times, but tonight we made the mistake of ordering our meal to go. A pretty simple order ... pizza, cheese garlic bread and a pork sausage sandwich. I arrived about 30 minutes after placing the order, waited 10 minutes and they brought out the pizza. But, I had to then wait another 30 minutes for the cheese garlic bread and sandwich and fries. The fries were already cold and rubbery and the sandwich was served plain (after requesting lettuce and tomato). We had to re-heat the pizza at home, discard the fries and dress up the sandwich. Not a great experience ...

I was wondering when happy hour was. Not because I wanted to drink at all, but because nobody was happy there. Service at this one has regularly been poor and pretty slow. But like most BWW's, the wings are still great.
Great staff good priced drinks and great energy highly recommend for a night out with the girls

So I decided to grab Wendy's on a Wednesday nite after work, I ordered the 2 for 5 deal with a spicy nugget and spicy chicken sandwich I also ordered a No 4 combo which is a big bacon classic large and an order of bacon jalapeño fries as well. The line wasn't too bad, the young lady that took my order wasn't pleasant/nice nor was she rude, I get it it's Wendy's you have lump them in w/McDonald's customer service/pleasantries go out the window as soon as step foot in the building or drive thru. I'd like to say my total was close to 20 dollars, I wasn't given a receipt and the reason for that is because they don't want you to go on-line and review the restaurant. I say all that to say this, this the 5th and last time won't deal with out being given a receipt ( scammer, double charge, or just plain old discrepancy with order such as this) I live about 10 mins away from this location so with a glance over the 3 bags I was given it appeared to be correct. Once I got home you already know where I'm headed with this. The 2 for 5 was incorrect and under counsel as wel. The chicken sandwich which was supposed to be spicy was a normal chicken patty without lettuce, the nuggets I was only given 6 it's a shame that I had too count but I did. The supposed big bacon classic combo was incorrect as well. People please understand the difference between the Jr bacon cheeseburger patty and a Dave's patty for a regular patty, I was a given a Jr bacon patty with no bacon or lettuce my jalapeño had little to cheese or no and I mean no jalapeno. There's no way to verify anything foodwise in the drive-thru. I wasn't able to verify a thing until I got home. Once I got home I threw the food away after realizing my order wasn't correct. Now I do understand that at these times there's a shortage as far as beef, change etc due to this Covid-19 ordeal but Please post signage or let customers know what's available versus what's not. I will google the location to find out the owner/general /district/regional manager are and let them know. Because this is just unacceptable these locations are fully aware of what the inventory is or isn't. Embarrassing point, blank period. If you read this review think twice before ordering anything from this location the overall staff isn't too be trusted. Please, please find a way to incorporate a kiosk to minimize the attitude and negativity of the workers ( i worked in fast food restaurants throughout HS and college with playing football and balancing scholastics you always have a choice gig/job/career wise) also to maximize the accuracy of the order, this staff clearly give little too no F's about any of the above.

I eat lunch poolside every time we visit Don Cesar and this time was no exception. It is pricey but what poolside resort restaurant isn't? The waitstaff is excellent. Our server Laura who came onto the pool deck to serve us was so friendly and attentive. She even made sure we had ice water as we relaxed at the pool. My husband and I started with drinks. Him, the classic frozen margarita; me, the Patron blueberry skinny margarita. Tasty and refreshing. We shared the tuna tartare ($10) served with a sesame seaweed slaw and spicy shrimp chips. The tuna was fresh, the slaw spicy and the chips light and airy. It was very small for two to share and they could have provided more chips. I think we had 5 chips served in a small bowl. Nix the bowl and put more chips on the plate. When we were ready for a late lunch, we shared the gulf coast fish tacos ($16). We asked for an additional taco so we had two each. They were accommodating and even split them on two plates for us. The tacos were very fresh with perfectly grilled fish, cilantro salsa, chipotle crema and served with a very tasty citrus jicama slaw. Seeing that we are staying all week at the Don Cesar, I will be exploring more of the menu. Also, if you just want to visit for lunch and are not staying at the resort, you'll enjoy the gulf breeze and wonderful view while you eat fresh fare.
I love this place. They have the BEST burnt ends in town. The prices have increased, but it is worth it!

This place is great. My husband wanted to go there after reading about it in a book. (Apparently there was a mob hit here in the 80's). Started with fried calamari, very crisp and not chewy. I ordered lasagna, it was enough for 3 people. My husband ordered a pasta seafood dish and he finished his plate. We will be sure to back if were ever in Philly again. Tip: order the tiramisu :)
Muffuletta. That. Is. All. :) A simple sandwich but very flavorful. Tried a slice of hubby's at the market. It's nothing fancy but it's not supposed to be either. The half feeds two easily.

A. Packed by 4pm B. Mussels and fries are a staple C. Way too much beer selection (that is a positive) D. Dark interior is a primo spot to impress a date E. Costs as much to eat/drink here as any other specialty spot F. Eating at the front bar is always an option if too long a wait for a table I will hit it again, but before 4pm.

Best restaurant on the beach! Years of meals at Guppy's and its always fabulous! The food is always delicious, great happy hour, and atmosphere is wonderful. Dining inside or on the patio is cozy and you can still carry on a conversation.
Foods good nd fresh made to order .. service is shitty rude . No hello can i help u , thanks have a good day .

I've eaten here several times and I can tell you it is a step above sports bar grub. The portions are excessive, so excessive that most diners walk out carrying an eco-unfriendly container with leftovers. I'd rather have a portion I can finish so I am not putting a Styrofoam container in a landfill. As stated, the bar food is typical sports bar grub. The pizza is by far the best thing on their menu and the wings come a close second. Both are perfect for sharing with a group of friends. My most recent lunch was a burger. I choose the Jalapeno which was stuffed with the spicy pepper and cover with Soft Cheddar Cheese with slices of Jalepeno Peppers. I enjoyed it, by the time I took my last bite I had little beads of sweat on my forehead. Sweat means those peppers were damn good. Next time I order it, I will have them hold the bun and give me half the cheese topping(remember, I said they do things in excess). The staff is friendly, but sometimes the service is slow as stated in other reviews. Slow service is okay if you're there watching a game, but when you want to get in and out for a work lunch it is not acceptable. Staff is easy to spot, they are all in neat black Joey B's t-shirts and the bartender is dressed in a Target Cami (good for getting bigger tips).

Make sure you have reservations for Seasons 52! When I finally got them, I came here on a Saturday as a party of three. I think what everyone really tells you is about the desserts. But anyway, we ordered the steak and mushroom flatbread. So tasty! Probably a bit tangy from the cheese but good in my book. Probably the best part of our meal. My bf ordered the chicken, I got the pork tenderloin and my friend got the lemongrass salmon salad. This is where the meal goes downhill. My pork was super super dry. The flavors did not come together well. The polenta was gross. Dishes like this make me hope that eating healthy doesn't really taste like this... The chicken was boring and a bit on the dry side as well. My friend really enjoyed her salad though. For dessert, we tried the key lime, peanut butter and the mocha. The key lime was by far the best. Although the desserts in a shot glass is such a gimmick. I'd bake my own key lime pie any day. This place is waay overrated. I think people just like the idea of eating 'healthy'.

Came here after work for happy hour with a few friends. I ordered the Alma sangria and my friend ordered a regular berry one. I tried her's and it was better than the Alma one so I'd recommend getting the berry sangria over the Alma. As for the food itself, I ordered a shrimp pasta dish which came out with a different pasta style than advertised and it seemed like it wouldn't be a cream based dish but was. It came with garlic bread and wasn't that filling, I was still hungry after and it was kind of pricey for the entree. Overall the ambiance was very much Floridian which was fun and they had TVs up as well as live music/singing. Normally I love live music but it was kind of hard to chat with friends since the layout of the restaurant is narrow and the music was overpowering everything. Definitely feel like this is a fun addition to the International mall area though

I went here on Mother's Day with my family and the service was so terrible it was an awful experience. Our waitress didn't come to our table until about 15 minutes after we arrived and then she forgot about our drinks so we didn't get them for another 15 minutes. She barely removed any of our dirty plates and she gave us the wrong bill twice and refused to split it up. The food was decent but it was extremely over priced at $35 a person not including drinks. I'm a server so I know what it's like to be short staffed but our server wasn't apologetic at all. I won't be going back.

Had a big petty here & the experience wasn't pleasure. The waiter insisted on reading the menu when the whole party hadn't even arrived yet. The food was pretty but my grandma cooks better. I would say only 1/5 of the plate had protein and the "salad" or vegetable pieces made up the rest of the plate. Can't relate & wouldn't recommend. Would've rather spent $700 at Hub down the street.
This restaurant lives up to the reviews. The food is plentiful and has great texture and flavor. The prices are extremely reasonable.
We love your restaurant but are so upset that you don't offer the Cubano any longer. Please add it, again, to your menu! We are locals and will add to your success. Thanks.

A Nola must stop! My favorite is the BBQ Shrimp! Words cannot describe the flavor! You just have to try it for yourself! The sweet tea is sugarlaide This place is a local "watering hole" very unique. Once you go once you'll have to come back time and time again!

I went on a Thursday afternoon for the lunch buffet and was not disappointed! We got there around 11:15 and there were plenty of open tables, with it being a little more crowded by the time we left. Of course everything is ready to go so when you walk in you can just go straight to the buffet - so this is a good quick spot. The buffet had a great variety and I had no problem filling my plate and going back up for more. It was all delicious and my boyfriend especially enjoyed the dessert options. It is is so reasonable at about $10/person total for all you can eat goodness. I would also mention that a large group of 10 or 12 people came in while we were there and barely made a dent in the food... they are prepared for crowds! We will certainly be back.

Don't waste your time the food is mediocore and the service awful any taco truck would be better. Why would you spend tour lifestyle savings to open up a POS restaurant. Mas chingon mas cagada is more like it.

The only thing I really enjoy about this place is the ambiance. When its nice outside sitting on the porch is really enjoyable especially when they have local bands playing outside. I have been here quite a few time to hang out and drink but I really have never had any food that I really liked or had to have again. I highly suggest checking this place out to watch local entertainment and have a few beers with friends but dont plan a date night dinner here.

This is my experience with spread. Walked in on Monday morning to a girl behind the counter who saw us, turned her back towards us and aimlessly looked for cream cheese. She went on a stunning amount of time pulling bagels out of the toaster and asking a guy who came out there things were. I wanted to leave but we went through so much trouble parking, we were screwed into staying. There were about 2 people waiting for sandwiches. We then ordered there breakfast sandwiches (all without meat) and 2 iced teas. The total was 33 dollars. Unreal pricing. I thought it could be a mistake but after waiting that long we just wanted to go. The sandwiches were just ok, nothing special. I have never witnessed customer service like this and after being ripped off, I won't return. There's SO many good spots in the city for bagels it would be a shame to go here. They no doubt continue to have business based on their prime location, nothing else.

My first meal in New Orleans on a quick visit & it was amazing. The service was great, pleasant and attentive host & waitress. I had the catfish & shrimp platter , was so much food I had some later that night. Will return when I visit again.

I used to like Limoncello, but it has gone downhill! Service was terrible. Waited 10 minutes for our waiter to take our drink order. Then it took another 10 minutes to get them to our table - even though we could see them sitting on the bar. Our bread and water was gone by the time he got back with them; I had to flag someone down every time we needed our water refilled. In fact, I had to flag down our waiter every time we needed something because he never checked in...but i watched him check in with his other tables! We ordered our apps, which came withing minutes so we waited a little bit to order dinner, thinking it would also come quickly. Boy were we wrong! It took 40 minutes for our entrees to arrive...and my husband meal was wrong. But there was no one to inform since the waiter was no where to be found. I was almost done my meal by the time I could get his attention to come and check in on us. He did take the meal off the bill. We'll never go back. There are too many other places in WC with great food and service.

Small as everyone here has noted but we had a good time. The food is all good. Great bread, appetizers and entrees. My grilfriend's gnocci melted in your mouth. My roommate ordered the lamb and was very impressed. It's probably my fault for ordering it, but I got the spaghetti bolognese and it was good, though not 5 star great. I guess I'm a bit picky! But a solid 4 to 4 1/2 stars for this great BYOB.
The food is delicious, service is friendly, and the prices are affordable. Really love their tortas.
We LOVE this dinner. Great food, nice atmosphere.Annie (our server) is fantastic! We come here and purposely request her.
Most chains,( which the area loves) are horrible. However, this place is great! Go try it, never a bad experience.

This is my boyfriend's favorite pupusas spot. Pupusas are authentic here! Tasty fresh and their plate with two pupusas rice and beans is like 8-9 dollars. It's a lot of food!!! Their curtido on the side tastes mm mm good!!! Next time I'm in the area I will definitely stop for pupusas.
